text:
Michael Kesselring has taken the long way to San Jose: a sixth-round pick of the Oilers in 2018, then Arizona, Utah and Buffalo before landing with the Sharks. At 6-foot-5, with a 93.7 mph shot (85th percentile in the NHL's tracking) and bursts of speed that rank in the 92nd percentile, he looks the part, and the Sharks are using him like it, at 19 minutes a night.

Three assists in 19 games doesn't jump off the page, but this is a case where the result undersells the process. With him on the ice, the Sharks have scored 4.8 fewer goals than their chances deserve, and a shortfall like that usually swings back. On a team that has lost five straight, the five-on-five numbers are also a touch better with him than without him.

Last season Evolving-Hockey had his competition in the 95th percentile, over a small 455-minute sample, which fits how he's being used. He isn't a puck-mover by trade, so don't expect a power-play role. We'd watch whether the assists start to arrive as the on-ice shooting evens out. Our projection has him around 14 points the rest of the way.
headline: Bad luck is hiding Michael Kesselring's steadier start
